children.description: Buddleja axillaris is a shrub endemic to Madagascar, the Comoro Islands, and Tanzania, growing in forests at elevations of 300–1400 m.

children.name: Buddleja bhutanica T.Yamaz.
children.description: Buddleja bhutanica is a species of flowering shrub endemic to Bhutan, where it grows in bush on mountain slopes at elevations around 1,700 m.

children.name: Buddleja blattaria J.F.Macbr.
children.description: Buddleja blattaria is a small shrub endemic to the regions of Piura and Cajamarca in northern Peru.

children.name: Buddleja bordignonii G.P.Coelho & Miotto
children.description: Buddleja bordignonii G.P.Coelho & Miotto — a magnoliopsida species in the genus Buddleja.

children.name: Buddleja brachiata Cham. & Schltdl.
children.description: Buddleja brachiata is endemic to southern Brazil from Goiás to São Paulo, where it grows on disturbed areas along rivers.

children.name: Buddleja brachystachya Diels
children.description: Buddleja brachystachya is a small shrub endemic to the Yunnan, Sichuan and Gansu provinces of China, where it grows on open, rocky, often dry, places at altitudes of 2,000–2,400 m.

children.name: Buddleja brasiliensis J.Jacq.
children.description: Buddleja brasiliensis J.Jacq. — a magnoliopsida species in the genus Buddleja.

children.name: Buddleja bullata Kunth
children.description: Buddleja bullata is a variable species endemic to the Andes, from Venezuela south through Colombia and Ecuador to Peru, at elevations of 1,800–3,600 m, where it grows on stream beds and in the remnants of montane forest.

children.name: Buddleja candida Dunn
children.description: Buddleja candida is a small deciduous shrub widely distributed from north-east India through south east Xizang (Tibet) to the provinces of Sichuan and Yunnan in western China, growing on forest edges, in mountain thickets, and along riverbanks, at altitudes of 1000–2500 m.

children.name: Buddleja cardenasii Standl. ex E.M.Norman
children.description: Buddleja cardenasii Standl. ex E.M.Norman — a magnoliopsida species in the genus Buddleja.

children.name: Buddleja cestriflora Cham.
children.description: Buddleja cestriflora is a rare species endemic to a small area near the eastern coast of Brazil, where it grows in the cloud forest along roadsides and in wet rocky clearings on the eastern border of Serra Geral of Santa Catarina and Rio Grande do Sul.

children.name: Buddleja chapalana B.L.Rob.
children.description: Buddleja chapalana is a rare species endemic to the rocky cliffs bordering the northern and western shores of Lake Chapala, Jalisco, Mexico.

children.name: Buddleja chenopodiifolia Kraenzl.
children.description: Buddleja chenopodiifolia is a species endemic to the dry rocky or clay hillsides of southern Peru at altitudes of 2200–3100 m; it was first described and named by Kraenzlin in 1913.

children.name: Buddleja columbiae André, 1901
children.description: Buddleja columbiae André, 1901 — a magnoliopsida species in the genus Buddleja.

children.name: Buddleja colvilei Hook.fil. & Thomson
children.description: Buddleja colvilei is endemic to the eastern Himalaya; discovered by Hooker in 1849, he declared it 'the handsomest of all Himalayan shrubs.' In 1896 the species was awarded the RHS First Class Certificate (FCC), given to plants 'of outstanding excellence for exhibition'.

children.name: Buddleja cordata Kunth
children.description: Buddleja cordata is endemic to Mexico, growing along forest edges and water courses at elevations of 1500–3000 m; it has also naturalized in parts of Ethiopia.

children.name: Buddleja cordobensis Griseb.
children.description: Buddleja cordobensis is a species of flowering plant in the family Scrophulariaceae.

children.name: Buddleja coriacea J.Rémy
children.description: Buddleja coriacea is a variable species endemic to the high Andes from the Cordillera Blanca in Peru to Lake Titicaca in Bolivia.

children.name: Buddleja corrugata M.E.Jones
children.description: Buddleja corrugata is a species endemic to north-western Mexico including the Baja California Sur, growing on limestone at altitudes of 200–1900 m; it was first described and named by Jones in 1933.

children.name: Buddleja crispa Benth.
children.description: Buddleja crispa, the Himalayan butterfly bush, is a deciduous shrub native to Iran, Afghanistan, Bhutan, North India, Nepal, Pakistan and China (Yunnan, Sichuan, Tibetan Autonomous Region and north to Gansu), where it grows on dry river beds, slopes with boulders, exposed cliffs, and in thickets, at altitudes of 1400–4300 m.

children.name: Buddleja crotonoides A.Gray
children.description: Buddleja crotonoides is a shrub with a wide distribution, from California south to Nicaragua.

children.name: Buddleja cuneata Cham.
children.description: Buddleja cuneata is a rare species endemic only to the southern plateau of Brazil, where it grows in dry and rocky fields from Paraná to Rio Grande do Sul.

children.name: Buddleja curviflora Hook. & Arn.
children.description: Buddleja curviflora is a deciduous shrub native to southern Japan and Taiwan, where it grows in thickets on stony slopes at elevations of 100–300 m.

children.name: Buddleja cuspidata Baker
children.description: Buddleja cuspidata is a species endemic to Madagascar, where it grows along river banks.

children.name: Buddleja davidii Franch.
children.description: Buddleja davidii (spelling variant Buddleia davidii), also called butterfly-bush, orange eye, or summer lilac, is a species of flowering plant in the family Scrophulariaceae, native to most of China except for the far northeast.

children.name: Buddleja delavayi L.F.Gagnep.
children.description: {{Speciesbox |image = Buddleja delavayii, general view.jpg |image_caption = Buddleja delavayi in May, Portchester, England.

children.name: Buddleja diffusa Ruiz & Pav.
children.description: Buddleja diffusa is a species of flowering plant in the family Scrophulariaceae.

children.name: Buddleja domingensis Urb.
children.description: Buddleja domingensis, also known as the Hispaniolan butterfly bush, is a species endemic to the high mountain ranges in the Caribbean island of Hispaniola (Haiti and the Dominican Republic), growing in rocky, limestone ravines, along forest edges and roadsides.

children.name: Buddleja dysophylla  Phillips
children.description: Buddleja dysophylla is a species endemic to southern Africa, from Zaire and Tanzania south to Malawi, and from the Transvaal to Eastern Cape Province, where it grows along forest edges or in scrub at elevations of 0–2,600 m.

children.name: Buddleja elegans Cham. & Schltdl.
children.description: Buddleja elegans Cham. & Schltdl. — a magnoliopsida species in the genus Buddleja.

children.name: Buddleja euryphylla Standl. & Steyerm.
children.description: Buddleja euryphylla is a species endemic to cloud forest in El Salvador, Guatemala and Honduras; it was first described and named by Standley and Steyermark in 1947.

children.name: Buddleja fallowiana Balf.fil. & W.W.Sm.
children.description: Buddleja fallowiana is a species of flowering plant in the figwort family Scrophulariaceae.

children.name: Buddleja filibracteolata J.A.González & J.F.Morales
children.description: Buddleja filibracteolata is a species of flowering plant in the family Scrophulariaceae, native to the rainforests of Costa Rica.

children.name: Buddleja forrestii Diels
children.description: Buddleja forrestii is a deciduous shrub or small tree widely distributed from India to western China.

children.name: Buddleja fragifera Leeuwenb.
children.description: Buddleja fragifera is a rare evergreen shrub endemic to the southern tip of Madagascar, where it grows amongst scrub near the coast.

children.name: Buddleja fusca Baker
children.description: Buddleja fusca is a species of flowering plant in the figwort family, Scrophulariaceae that is endemic to Madagascar.

children.name: Buddleja glaberrima Hort.Amat.
children.description: Buddleja glaberrima Hort.Amat. — a magnoliopsida species in the genus Buddleja.

children.name: Buddleja globosa Hope
children.description: Buddleja globosa, also known as the orange-ball-tree, orange ball buddleja, and matico, is a species of flowering plant native to Chile and Argentina, where it grows in dry and moist forest, from sea level to 2,000 m.

children.name: Buddleja glomerata H.Wendl.
children.description: Buddleja glomerata is a shrub endemic to the mountains of the Karoo desert in South Africa, where it grows among boulders on dry hillsides.

children.name: Buddleja grandiflora Cham. & Schltdl.
children.description: Buddleja grandiflora is endemic to the marshy fields and river margins of southern Brazil, and adjacent areas of Argentina and Uruguay.

children.name: Buddleja gujanensis Roxb.
children.description: Buddleja gujanensis Roxb. — a magnoliopsida species in the genus Buddleja.

children.name: Buddleja hatschbachii E.M.Norman & L.B.Sm.
children.description: Buddleja hatschbachii is a rare species found only in the wet ravines and rock slopes flanking the east side of the planalto of southern Brazil.

children.name: Buddleja hieronymi R.E.Fr.
children.description: Buddleja hieronymi is a species endemic to southern Bolivia and northern Argentina first described and named by Fries in 1905.

children.name: Buddleja ibarrensis E.M.Norman
children.description: Buddleja ibarrensis is an endangered species endemic to a small area of Ecuador in the vicinity of Ibarra in subtropical or tropical moist montane forest at an elevation of 2,200 m threatened by deforestation.

children.description: Buddleja incompta L.fil. — a magnoliopsida species in the genus Buddleja.

children.name: Buddleja indica Lam.
children.description: Buddleja indica is an evergreen shrub native to Madagascar, the Comoro Islands, and the Mascarene Islands, where it grows from the coast into the mountains up to elevations of 2000 m in either scrub or clearings.

children.name: Buddleja indica x madagascariensis
children.description: Buddleja indica is an evergreen shrub native to Madagascar, the Comoro Islands, and the Mascarene Islands, where it grows from the coast into the mountains up to elevations of 2000 m in either scrub or clearings.

children.name: Buddleja interrupta Kunth
children.description: Buddleja interrupta is a species endemic to the dry valleys and roadsides of northern Peru at altitudes < 2600 m.

children.description: Buddleja iresinoides is a species of flowering plant in the family Scrophulariaceae.

children.name: Buddleja jamesonii Benth.
children.description: Buddleja jamesonii is a species endemic to southern Ecuador, where it grows in moist, protected ravines and borders of tussocks at elevations of 3,000 – 4,000 m.

children.name: Buddleja japonica Hemsl.
children.description: Buddleja japonica is a deciduous shrub in the family Scrophulariaceae.

children.name: Buddleja jinsixiaensis R.B.Zhu
children.description: Buddleja jinsixiaensis is a newly discovered species endemic to Shaanxi, China, where it grows in the Jinxia Grand Canyon at an elevation of c.

children.name: Buddleja kleinii E.M.Norman & L.B.Sm.
children.description: Buddleja kleinii is a species endemic to a small area of cloud forest bordering the eastern portion of the Serra Geral of Santa Catarina and the Rio Grande do Sul in Brazil at altitudes of 1200 – 1650 m.

children.name: Buddleja lanata Benth.
children.description: Buddleja lanata is a species endemic to Ecuador where it grows on dry, windy plateaux amid grasses and bracken at elevations of 1,150 – 2,700 m.

children.name: Buddleja lindleyana Fortune ex Lindl.
children.description: Buddleja lindleyana is a deciduous shrub native to the provinces of Anhui, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangsu, Shanghai, Sichuan, and Yunnan in China, where it grows in rocky scrub alongside streams and tracks at elevations of 200 – 2700 m.

children.name: Buddleja lojensis E.M.Norman
children.description: Buddleja lojensis is a species endemic to the Loja region of southern Ecuador, and Piura in Peru, where it grows on mountains, savannahs and scrub, notably near streams, at elevations of 1,600 – 2,550 m.

children.name: Buddleja longiflora Brade
children.description: Buddleja longiflora is a rare species of flowering plant in the family Scrophulariaceae.

children.name: Buddleja longifolia Kunth
children.description: Buddleja longifolia is a species now restricted to remnants of montane forest in Loja, Ecuador, and northern Peru at altitudes of 2100 – 2600 m.

children.name: Buddleja loricata Leeuwenb.
children.description: Buddleja loricata is a hardy evergreen shrub endemic to South Africa and Mozambique, where it grows on mountain slopes at elevations above 1,800 m.

children.name: Buddleja macrostachya Wall. ex Benth.
children.description: Buddleja macrostachya is a large deciduous shrub or small tree with a vast distribution, from Xizang (Tibet) through western China, Bhutan, Sikkim, northern India, Bangladesh, Myanmar (Burma), to Thailand and Vietnam, growing in scrub on mountain slopes to an altitude of 3,200 m, and along rivers in forests.

children.name: Buddleja madagascariensis Lam.
children.description: Buddleja madagascariensis, the smokebush or Madagascan butterfly bush, is a species of flowering plant in the figwort family Scrophulariaceae.

children.name: Buddleja marrubiifolia Benth.
children.description: Buddleja marrubiifolia, commonly known as the woolly butterflybush, is a perennial shrub which is endemic to the Chihuahuan Desert from southern Texas to San Luis Potosí in Mexico, where it grows on limestone and gypsum soils in canyons and arroyos at elevations of elevation.

children.name: Buddleja megalocephala Donn.Sm.
children.description: Buddleja megalocephala is a species endemic to Guatemala, in the Central Highlands, the Sierra de los Cuchumatanes, and Mt.

children.name: Buddleja mendozensis Gillies ex Benth.
children.description: Buddleja mendozensis is an extremely variable species endemic to the xeric and subxeric areas of Argentina, from Jujuy to southern Mendoza and La Pampa, where it grows on rocks at altitudes of 600 – 3,000 m.

children.name: Buddleja mendozinensis Gillies ex Benth., 1846
children.description: Buddleja mendozinensis Gillies ex Benth., 1846 — a magnoliopsida species in the genus Buddleja.

children.name: Buddleja microstachya E.D.Liu & H.Peng
children.description: Buddleja microstachya is a small shrub discovered in 2005 by Liu and Peng in Yunnan, China, growing at an elevation of 3,200 m in rocky terrain of the Yongde Mountains Nature Reserve.

children.name: Buddleja misionum Kraenzl.
children.description: Buddleja misionum is a species endemic to dry rocky fields and roadsides in southern Paraguay, the Rio Grande do Sul in Brazil, and the provinces of Corrientes and Misiones in Argentina; it was first described and named by Kraenzlin in 1913.

children.name: Buddleja montana Britton
children.description: Buddleja montana is a species endemic to the rocky hillsides of the cordilleras of Peru at altitudes of 2,700 – 4,000 m, extending into Bolivia; it was named and described by Britton in 1898.

children.name: Buddleja multiceps Kraenzl.
children.description: Buddleja multiceps Kraenzl. — a magnoliopsida species in the genus Buddleja.

children.name: Buddleja myriantha Diels
children.description: Buddleja myriantha is a species endemic to upper Burma and western China, including Tibet, where it grows along forest edges, thickets and streams at altitudes of 2,000 – 3,200 m.

children.name: Buddleja neemda Buch.-Ham., 1832
children.description: Buddleja neemda Buch.-Ham., 1832 — a magnoliopsida species in the genus Buddleja.

children.name: Buddleja nitida Benth.
children.description: Buddleja nitida is a species endemic to much of Central America, from southern Chiapas in Mexico south to the Sierra de Talamanca in northern Panama, where it grows on limestone slopes, in cloud forest, in clearings and pastures at altitudes of 2,000 – 4,000 m.

children.name: Buddleja nivea Duthie
children.description: Buddleja nivea is a vigorous shrub endemic to western China, evergreen in the wild, but deciduous in cultivation in the UK.

children.name: Buddleja normaniae J.H.Chau
children.description: Buddleja normaniae J.H.Chau — a magnoliopsida species in the genus Buddleja.

children.name: Buddleja oblonga Benth.
children.description: Buddleja oblonga is a species endemic to the Serra do Caparaó and south as far as Paraná in Brazil, where it grows in fields and damp thickets near streams at altitudes of 1,000 – 2,200 m.

children.name: Buddleja officinalis Maxim.
children.description: Buddleja officinalis is a deciduous early-spring flowering shrub native to west Hubei, Sichuan, and Yunnan provinces in China.

children.name: Buddleja paniculata Wall.
children.description: Buddleja paniculata is a species of flowering plant in the figwort family Scrophulariaceae, endemic to a wide upland area from northern India to Bhutan, growing along forest margins, in thickets, and on rocky slopes at elevations of .

children.name: Buddleja parviflora Kunth
children.description: Buddleja parviflora is large dioecious shrub or small tree endemic to much of upland Mexico north of the Isthmus of Tehuantepec, in forests at elevations of 750 – 3500 m.

children.name: Buddleja perfoliata Kunth
children.description: Buddleja perfoliata is endemic to the xerophytic and subzerophytic grasslands of central Mexico at elevations of 1500 – 2700 m.

children.name: Buddleja pichinchensis Kunth
children.description: Buddleja pichinchensis is endemic to the southern Cordillera Central of Colombia and the northern and central highlands of Ecuador, where it grows with Escallonia in páramo and subparamo regions at altitudes of 3,300 – 4,200 m.

children.name: Buddleja polycephala Kunth
children.description: Buddleja polycephala is a shrub endemic to southern Ecuador and areas around Ayabaca and Piura, and Cajamarca in Peru, at elevations of 2,000 – 2,700 m.

children.name: Buddleja polystachya Fresen.
children.description: Buddleja polystachya is a multi-branched shrub or occasionally small tree endemic to the semi-arid highlands flanking the Red Sea in Eritrea, Ethiopia, Saudi Arabia, Somalia and Yemen, where it grows in secondary scrub or around forest, often along watercourses, at elevations of between 2,200 and 3,600 m; its range extends southward into the highlands of Kenya and Tanzania.

children.name: Buddleja pulchella N.E.Br.
children.description: Buddleja pulchella is endemic to the open mountain forest of South Africa, Zimbabwe, Kenya and Tanzania at elevations of 1,200 – 2,000 m.

children.name: Buddleja racemosa A.Gray
children.description: Buddleja racemosa, commonly known as the Wand (or Texas) Butterfly Bush, is endemic to the southern edge of the limestone Edwards Plateau in Texas, United States, from Austin to Rocksprings, growing around streams, creeks and springs at elevations of 250 – 750 m.

children.name: Buddleja ramboi L.B.Sm.
children.description: Buddleja ramboi is a very rare Brazilian species found only infrequently in the shrubby or grassy fields of Santa Catarina and Rio Grande do Sul.

children.name: Buddleja rinconensis  J.H.Chau
children.description: Buddleja rinconensis  J.H.Chau — a magnoliopsida species in the genus Buddleja.

children.name: Buddleja rufescens Willd. ex Roem. & Schult.
children.description: Buddleja rufescens is endemic to western Peru from Piura to Ica where it grows along roadsides, dry river courses, and in remnants of scrubby woodland from sea level to 2,000 m.

children.name: Buddleja saligna Willd.
children.description: Buddleja saligna, the false olive or bastard olive, is native to South Africa and Zimbabwe, where it has a wide distribution.

children.name: Buddleja salviifolia  Lam.
children.description: Buddleja salviifolia, common names sage bush and sagewood, is endemic to much of southern and eastern Africa, from Kenya and Angola south, where it grows on rocky hillsides, along forest margins and watercourses.

children.name: Buddleja scordioides Kunth
children.description: Buddleja scordioides is endemic to central Arizona, southeastern New Mexico, southwestern Texas, and the Chihuahua Desert of Mexico, growing amidst xeric thorn-scrub on alkaline soils at elevations of 600 – 2,500 m.

children.name: Buddleja sessiliflora Kunth
children.description: Buddleja sessiliflora, commonly known as Rio Grande butterfly-bush or tepozán, native to southern Arizona and the lower Rio Grande Valley of Texas in the United States as well as much of central and northern Mexico excluding the Chihuahua Desert and Baja California Sur.

children.name: Buddleja skutchii C.V.Morton
children.description: Buddleja skutchii is endemic to much of the sierras of Central America, growing mostly in pine-oak forest, also in cloud forest, and in shrubby secondary growth.

children.name: Buddleja soratae Kraenzl.
children.description: Buddleja soratae is a rare species endemic to one small area of Bolivia around Sorata, growing along forest edges at altitudes of 2,700 – 3,200 m; it was first described and named by Kraenzlin in 1913.

children.name: Buddleja speciosissima Taub.
children.description: Buddleja speciosissima is a rare species restricted to Mount Itatiaia in Brazil, where it grows in rocky grassland at elevations of 2,000–2,500 m.

children.description: Buddleja stachyoides is the most widespread member of the genus in South America, endemic to woodland edges, roadsides and riversides in Argentina, Brazil, Bolivia, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

children.name: Buddleja suaveolens Kunth & C.D.Bouché

children.description: Buddleja tubiflora is endemic to much of northern Argentina, southern Paraguay, and southern Brazil, where it grows at the edge of woodlands, thickets, and in old fields, at low elevations.

children.description: Buddleja utahensis is a species of Buddleja endemic to the southwestern United States (northwest Arizona, eastern California, southern Nevada, and southwestern Utah), where it is often found in association with Joshua trees.

children.name: Lyperia antirrhinoides  Hilliard
children.description: Frozen plants (100 g) were blended with EtOH (300 ml) filtered and taken to dryness, and partitioned between H 2 O and Et 2 O. The aqueous phase was concentrated (1.6 g) and subjected to C 18 reverse-phase chromatography (Lobar size C), eluting with MeOH – H 2 O mixtures. Aucubin (2) and melittoside (3) was eluted with 25: 1 while 8 - O- acetylharpagide (4) was eluted with 3: 1. Unfortunately the amounts of the isolated compounds were not recorded. NMR spectra of the compounds are given in SI.
